chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying, and he mentioned the prayer of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family):

Water for ablution was brought to him and covered near his head, and his miswak was placed under his bed. Then he slept as much as Allah willed. When he woke up, he sat up, cast his gaze toward the sky, then recited the verses from Surah Ali 'Imran: 'Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day...' [the verse]. Then he brushed his teeth and purified himself, then went to the mosque and bowed in four rak'ahs. His bowing was proportional to his recitation, and his prostration was proportional to his bowing. He would bow until it was said, 'When will he raise his head?' and he would prostrate until it was said, 'When will he raise his head?' Then he returned to his bed and slept as much as Allah willed.

Then he woke up, sat, recited the verses from Surah Ali 'Imran, cast his gaze toward the sky, then brushed his teeth and purified himself, and went to the mosque to pray four rak'ahs just as he had prayed before. Then he returned to his bed and slept as much as Allah willed.

Then he woke up, sat, recited the verses from Surah Ali 'Imran, cast his gaze toward the sky, then brushed his teeth and purified himself, and went to the mosque to offer Witr and pray the two rak'ahs, then he went out for the congregational prayer.'
ai.seo_question: What is the step-by-step procedure for performing the night prayer (Tahajjud) as described in Shia hadith sources?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the Prophet’s (and Imam al-Sadiq’s) disciplined Tahajjud routine, emphasizing the spiritual preparation of reciting Surah Ali 'Imran verses 190-191 while contemplating creation before engaging in prolonged, meditative prayer. The practice highlights the Shia emphasis on integrating intellectual reflection (*tadabbur*) with physical worship, where the length of bowing and prostration reflects deep humility and presence of heart. This structured approach to night prayer serves as a model for believers to cultivate spiritual vigilance and connection with the Divine through consistent, mindful devotion.
